Today, Apple updated the Mac mini and Mac Studio, bringing Wi-Fi 7 support to these two product lines for the first time. Below is the complete list of Apple devices that support the full suite of Wi-Fi 7 features.

6 GHz band operation is not available in all regions.

Apple today published a support document detailing which of its products fully support Wi-Fi 7.

This list is different from Apple's broader list of devices capable of connecting to Wi-Fi 7 networks, since Wi-Fi 7 is backwards compatible.

That means devices that only support Wi-Fi 6E can still join a compatible Wi-Fi 7 network and use the 6 GHz band where available, even though they don't support the full set of Wi-Fi 7 features.

Wi-Fi 7 features include 320 MHz channels, 4096-QAM, and Multi-Link Operation (MLO), which deliver higher throughput, improved efficiency, and reduced latency; you can learn more here.

With that said, here's the list of devices that Apple officially says support the full suite of Wi-Fi 7 features as of August 2026:

  • MacBook Pro with the M5 Pro or M5 Max chip or later
  • MacBook Air with the M5 chip or later
  • Mac mini with the M5 Pro chip or later
  • Mac Studio with the M5 Max chip or later
  • iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, or later (not including iPhone 16e, iPhone 17e)
  • iPhone Air
  • iPad Pro with the M5 chip or later
  • iPad Air with the M4 chip or later

Apple notes that "Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 features operating in the 6 GHz band are only available in regions where the spectrum allows unlicensed Wi-Fi use," and adds that "if your region hasn't approved this kind of operation, your device will only use the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands to connect to Wi-Fi."
